result:
Here are the outcomes for staging `sec-filing-index-ingestion` from scratch. I haven't written any roadmap text yet.

## Outcomes (unranked)

The candidates come from the spec's rulings (§3) and scope (§2.1).

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A canonical filing-index Parquet for one real archived quarter, with provenance per row | R1, R3, §4.5 row contract | One SEC request. File size unknown; the probe below would measure it |
| O2 | A historical baseline over a quarter range you choose, with every quarter reported as complete, pending or failed | R1, §4.2 Backfill | Requests are trivial: about 135 quarterly files since 1993 is under a minute at 3 req/s. Data volume is unknown until O1's file size is known. Your time: golden fixtures for every historical format in the range (§4.6). This grows with how far back the range goes |
| O3 | Daily indexes added on top of the baseline, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2, §4.2 Daily | About 250 daily files a year, so requests are trivial. Size per file is unknown |
| O4 | Re-running a changed parser from stored raw bytes, with no new SEC download and no duplicate filings | R6 | Storage roughly doubles, because raw files and observations are both kept. No extra SEC traffic |
| O5 | Readers only ever see complete quarter generations, found through one active pointer, never by globbing | R9, §4.6 Publish | No material cost |
| O6 | A weekly re-check of quarterly indexes that records additions and field changes | R7, §4.4 | About 135 requests per run at your range's size |
| O7 | Closed-quarter removals held until you approve that exact source hash | R10 | Your time per approval. How often removals happen is unknown until O6 runs on real data |
| O8 | All SEC traffic (backfill, daily and re-check) shares one throttled budget, with a halt when access is denied | R8, §4.3 | No material cost |
| O9 | The above running on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, plus alerts and runbooks | R4, §4.7–4.9 | Azure dollars can't be estimated without region and sizing (§4.8). The §7 step-4 smoke test measures them |

I've treated R5 (shared code) and R11 (stated defaults) as project-wide constraints rather than outcomes. They're under "Choices already made" below.

## Tracks

**Track A, one known progression.** I considered putting the Azure work (O9) in its own track. I decided against it because O9 deploys the same catalog for the same use; it doesn't answer a separate question. It becomes the later stages of this one track, after the catalog works locally on real SEC data. That way the first real catalog doesn't wait on ADF machinery. The spec and its §7 exit procedure lay out the steps from the first quarter through scheduled operation, so I've labeled the track a known progression rather than research.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, in a uv workspace with four packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`, `-ingest`).
- Azure services per R4 and the ADR. Both the ADR and the spec are still **Proposed**, not accepted.
- One shared downloader, parser and publisher across backfill, daily and re-check (R5).
- §4.8 defaults are starting values, such as 3 req/s, 5 attempts and 05:00 ET daily (R11).
- The SEC User-Agent must identify you (§4.3). You'd need to give me the organization name and contact email; I won't fill them in myself.

## Proposed name

The spec's stem is used whole: `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`.

## One request

Please:
1. Rank O1–O9.
2. Confirm the single known-progression track, or split it.
3. Confirm the roadmap name.
4. Confirm whether to treat the Azure choice as settled while the ADR is still Proposed.

**Optional probe:** if you say yes and give me a User-Agent string, I'll download one archived quarter's `master.idx` (a single request). That would turn the "unknown size" cost notes into real figures before I write the stages.
